content.text:
**Finding: missing (medium) — no post-termination transition assistance or data return.**

Investigation summary:
- **Section 10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination)** covers only access cut-off (10.1), Deliverable delivery and refunds (10.2). Section 10.1 refers to "any agreed transition period" but creates no obligation to provide one.
- **Section 16.5** requires return/destruction of Confidential Information but expressly carves out Customer Data as "governed by Sections 11 and 15" — Section 11 does not exist in the document, and Section 15 contains only processing-purpose limits (15.1) and privacy compliance (15.2), with no return, export or deletion duty.
- Full-text searches for "transition", "export", "return" and "delet" confirmed there is no data-return, data-export or deletion-certification language anywhere in the Agreement — the walk-away risk of no data return on exit.

Redline (validated, ok:true): new **Section 10.3** inserted after 10.2, tracking the preferred position — up to six months' transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter (with the routine-backup/legal-retention carve-out already conceded in Section 16.5, so it should be uncontroversial). The comment offers the 90-day fallback if Vendor resists six months.
